title: Private Deployment: Network & Upgrade Acceptance Criteria for Closed-Loop Environments
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description: PRD fragment and acceptance criteria for Private/VPC installations that operate in closed-loop (limited or no egress) environments. Scope covers networking constraints, offline artifact mirroring, image provenance & signature verification, upgrade orchestration (online/offline), operational pre-checks, rollback behavior, and observability requirements for on-prem and VPC customers who cannot allow unrestricted outbound connectivity.
acceptance_criteria: Network: Document a minimal whitelist of external endpoints and ports required when operating in 'restricted-eject' mode. Primary allowed hosts must be configurable; default allowed: internal registry mirror, KMS (if using managed service), time-sync (NTP), and optionally a signed artifact mirror. Ports allowed must be explicit (e.g., 443/2376/5000).

Offline artifacts: Installer and runtime must support a local mirror flow where all container images and release artifacts are pulled from an on-prem mirror or airgapped bundle. Validate via a full install with no internet connectivity except to configured mirror host. Install passes end-to-end and components start successfully.

Image & artifact verification: All images and artifacts must be verified via signed manifests (GPG/DSSE or similar) before deployment. Acceptance test: tamper an artifact signature and verify the install aborts with a clear error code and remediation link.

Upgrade orchestration: Support both online rolling upgrades and offline image-swap upgrades. For rolling upgrades, the controller must perform a staged canary on 5% of nodes, run health checks, then continue in increments. A failed health check must automatically pause and optionally rollback. Validate: intentionally fail health probe on canary and confirm controller stops rollout and notifies via console/alerting.

Zero-implicit-egress: The platform must provide an 'offline-mode' toggle that prevents any unexpected outbound connection. Acceptance: run runtime in offline-mode and assert no outbound connections to hosts not whitelisted. Network tap or egress logs should show zero connections beyond the allowed set.

Deterministic rollback: If an upgrade fails post-canary, the system must be able to rollback to the previously pinned model/runtime image within the same upgrade window and re-open traffic. Validate rollback time-window and success rate in test environment (target: >95% automatic rollback success within 10 minutes).

Operational pre-checks: Upgrader must fail fast with descriptive errors when preconditions are unmet (insufficient disk, mismatched kernel features, missing mirror credentials, expired certs). Acceptance: introduce a precondition failure and verify upgrade aborts with remediation guidance in logs and Console UI.

Certificate & KMS: Certificate rotation and KMS key usage must work when key material is only available via an internal HSM/KMS over private network. Validate: rotate certificates and KMS keys without requiring public internet; verify zero-secret-leak and successful service restart.

Observability & auditing: Upgrade events, artifact checksums, and signature verification results must be logged to the audit stream (customer-accessible). Acceptance: run an upgrade and verify audit entries contain artifact checksums, signer identity, and upgrade outcome status.

Simulated airgap test: A runbook and automated test harness must exist that recreates an air-gapped customer environment, performs a full install and upgrade, and produces a pass/fail report. Test must include loss-of-egress scenarios and mirror sync failure cases.
Compatibility matrix: Provide clear compatibility table for supported OS, container runtimes, and minimum kernel versions. Acceptance: run smoke tests on each supported runtime and record pass/fail.

Image provenance: Require cryptographic provenance metadata (build id, git hash, builder image) attached to every release. Acceptance: verify UI and API surface surfaces provenance for each deployed image.

Time/Clock dependencies: Define fallback behavior when NTP/chrony cannot reach public time servers; platform must support using a local NTP server or hardware time source. Acceptance: run tests with blocked public NTP and verify components accept the local time source without error.

Upgrade window & maintenance mode: Platform must allow customers to define maintenance windows and must not perform automated upgrades outside configured windows. Acceptance: set a maintenance window and attempt an automated upgrade outside it; upgrade must be deferred and logged with reason.

Partial-connectivity recovery: When a mirror becomes unavailable mid-upgrade, the system must either gracefully pause and resume when mirror is restored or fall back to a previously fetched image cache if allowed. Acceptance: simulate mirror outage and verify deterministic behavior per configuration.

Backwards compatibility: All upgrades must support a documented rollback path to the previous major runtime within 30 days of release without requiring manual DB migrations. Acceptance: perform a rollback in test cluster and validate no data loss for user-level metadata and KV caches required for serving correctness.

Admin UX: Console must surface upgrade pre-check results, required egress endpoints, and a downloadable remediation checklist for customers that fail pre-checks. Acceptance: from Console, display failing pre-check with link to remediation and verify PM/Docs link works.

Security posture: All network egress policies and artifact verification flow must be covered in a security review and threat model before GA. Acceptance: security review ticket exists and is marked resolved with reviewer comments attached.

Performance safety: During rolling upgrades, percent increase in 95th percentile latency must be bounded (target: <10% regression). Acceptance: run load test during upgrade and measure latency impact against baseline.

Customer support playbooks: Provide an operational runbook that support engineers can follow for common failure modes (mirror sync failures, KMS auth, signature mismatch). Acceptance: runbook verified by support team and used in two dry-run drills.

Metrics & alerts: Emit metrics for artifact-verify failures, mirror sync errors, upgrade progress and rollback triggers. Acceptance: create dashboards and alert rules, then trigger a simulated failure and verify alert fires.

Legal/compliance: Provide guidance and attestations for customers requiring data residency; include explicit contract language for image provenance and SLSA provenance where applicable. Acceptance: legal signoff on the guidance document.

Minimal egress list: Provide default CIDR/IP list and ports required for optional components (e.g., image-staging, telemetry opt-in). Acceptance: documentation lists per-component egress and a validated minimal list used in install tests.
steps_to_validate: 1) Create an airgap mirror by exporting release artifacts to a private registry and a signed-bundle file.
2) Install a fresh cluster using only the private mirror (block all public outbound traffic). Verify install completes and services return healthy.
3) Run an upgrade using an offline bundle (no ingress to public registries). Intentionally modify one artifact signature to validate verification rejection.
4) Run a rolling upgrade with a failing canary health probe and confirm automated pause and rollback triggers.
5) Perform a KMS-based key rotation using on-prem HSM and verify secrets are still decryptable by runtime.
6) Execute simulated mirror outage during an upgrade and confirm system behavior matches configured policy (pause/resume or fallback to cache).
7) Validate observability: confirm audit events contain checksums, signer ID, and upgrade result.
8) Run load generator across the cluster while performing upgrade and check P95 latency regression under <10%.
9) Verify maintenance window prevents automated upgrades outside allowed time.
notes: Scope change: earlier drafts allowed 'best-effort' egress for telemetry; decision on 2025-02-25 to require explicit opt-in for telemetry with a documented minimal egress set.
Trade-offs: supporting both fully air-gapped and low-egress mirrored flows increases test matrix and QA time; prioritized coverage for common enterprise topologies (registry mirror + internal KMS).
Open question: how to surface signature verification failures in a way that non-SRE customers can remediate — proposed: inline remediation playbook + downloadable bundle.
